document_summary: New Jersey P.L. 2026, c.43 (the FAIR Act), approved July 20, 2026, makes it an antitrust violation to use or operate algorithmic rent-setting coordination software; it applies statewide in New Jersey.

rules.title: Forbidding the Algorithmic Inflation of Rent (FAIR) Act
rules.requirement: It is unlawful, and a violation of the New Jersey Antitrust Act, for rental property owners to pay for or use a coordinator's services, for coordinators to facilitate agreements restricting competition, for persons to engage in or facilitate parallel pricing coordination, or for any person to perform a coordinating function (algorithmic setting or recommendation of rents, lease terms or occupancy using shared competitively sensitive information).
rules.key_value: Ban on algorithmic coordination of rental prices, material lease terms and occupancy levels
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to rental property owners (persons owning one or more rental residential dwelling units, including controlling-interest holders), coordinators (operators of algorithmic revenue management software or algorithmic devices performing a coordinating function) and any person; residential dwelling units are units intended as a primary residence in the State.
rules.exemptions: Excluded from 'coordinating function': research, statistical analysis or testing not used to set or recommend prices or terms; free public rent estimates; real estate brokerage databases available on equal terms that do not set or recommend prices; government entities setting or limiting rents through affordability controls. Residential dwelling unit excludes inpatient medical care, licensed long-term care, and detention or correctional facilities. Spreadsheets without AI that require human analysis, and databases that only query unprocessed data, are not algorithmic devices.
rules.interaction: Section 6(b) prohibits a municipality from enacting an ordinance that conflicts with this act (except ordinances explicitly authorized or required by other law). The act supplements and does not limit the New Jersey Antitrust Act, P.L.1970, c.73; the Antitrust Act's enforcement provisions (sections 6-17) apply to violations.
rules.quoted_span: any person to perform a coordinating function.
rules.extraction_notes: Effective date computed from section 9 ('first day of the twelfth month next following the date of enactment') with approval on July 20, 2026: the first month following is August 2026, so the twelfth is July 2027, giving 2027-07-01. This is after the query date of 2026-10-01, so the status is not_yet_effective. The document is the first reprint of the bill, with the statutory text and chapter number as shown. Codification range C.56:9-20 to 56:9-26 is taken from the header.
